source: NCERT-aligned UPSC Ecology & Environment (Class XI), Ch. 10 (IUCN Red List, Endangered Species and Conservation Efforts).

sections.heading: 1. IUCN and the Red List
points: **IUCN (International Union for Conservation of Nature)** maintains the **Red List** — the global inventory of the **conservation status** of species.
It is the most comprehensive source on the risk of extinction of species.

sections.heading: 2. Red List Categories

sub: **Least Concern → Near Threatened → Vulnerable → Endangered → Critically Endangered → Extinct in the Wild → Extinct**.

points: **Vulnerable, Endangered, Critically Endangered** together = 'threatened' species.
**Critically Endangered** = highest risk of extinction in the wild.

sections.heading: 3. Endangered Species of India (Examples)
points: **Critically Endangered:** Great Indian Bustard, Gharial, Pygmy Hog, Jenkin's/Namdapha flying squirrel, Kashmir stag (Hangul), some vultures.
**Endangered:** Bengal tiger, Asiatic lion, Red panda, Blackbuck (near threatened), Snow leopard (vulnerable).
**Vulnerable:** Gangetic dolphin, Sloth bear, etc.
Causes: habitat loss, poaching, pollution, human-wildlife conflict.

sections.heading: 4. Conservation Efforts
points: **In-situ** (protected areas, projects) and **ex-situ** (zoos, captive breeding, gene banks) conservation.
Species recovery programmes; **Project Tiger/Elephant/Great Indian Bustard**; the **cheetah reintroduction (Kuno)**.
Legal protection under the **Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972 (Schedules)** and **CITES** for trade.
Community participation and awareness are vital.

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: IUCN Red List = global conservation status of species.
Categories: Least Concern → Near Threatened → Vulnerable → Endangered → Critically Endangered → Extinct in Wild → Extinct.
Threatened = Vulnerable + Endangered + Critically Endangered.
Critically Endangered (India): Great Indian Bustard, Gharial, Pygmy Hog, Hangul.
Conservation: in-situ + ex-situ; Wildlife Protection Act (1972) + CITES.

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: The **IUCN maintains the Red List** (species status).
Order of risk: **Vulnerable < Endangered < Critically Endangered** (CR = highest risk).
'**Threatened**' includes **Vulnerable, Endangered AND Critically Endangered**.
**Extinct in the Wild ≠ Extinct** (survives only in captivity).
